events.article: Work has begun in earnest upon the small post established on the ground recently added to Gaius Maximus Valerius's estate. Timber structures, repaired earthworks, storage shelters, and more durable approaches are being installed around the former expedition camp. The works remain modest and are not comparable with the permanent fortifications of a Roman military station, but they are intended to survive ordinary seasons rather than serve for a single campaign. The higher ground is being kept clear, while the road and water approaches are being maintained so that men and supplies can reach the post without difficulty. The new holding is consequently beginning to look less like an abandoned battlefield position and more like a permanent part of the estate.

events.article: Greater attention is now being given to the men wounded during the expedition against the robbers. Those unable to return to duty have been separated from the fit men and given places where they can be watched and treated without interfering with the daily work of the estate. Food, water, bandages, and rest have been provided more regularly, while men familiar with treating wounds have been assigned to the injured. Valerius has made clear that the expedition is to be preserved rather than rushed forward at the cost of men who may yet recover. The prospect of resuming operations has therefore become a practical concern around the estate, with the wounded regarded as future members of the company rather than simply losses from the recent battles.

events.article: The month closes with substantial changes visible upon the lands of Gaius Maximus Valerius.
